q1: SELECT MAX(NUM) AS NUM FROM (SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM HAVING COUNT(NUM) = 1) AS T
q2: SELECT IFNULL((SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM HAVING COUNT(NUM) =1 ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1), NULL) AS NUM
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT MAX(NUM) AS NUM FROM (SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM HAVING COUNT(NUM) = 1) AS T
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT IFNULL((SELECT NUM FROM MYNUMBERS GROUP BY NUM HAVING COUNT(NUM) =1 ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1), NULL) AS NUM
explanation: Both queries aim to retrieve the maximum number from the MYNUMBERS table that appears exactly once. Q1 does this by grouping, filtering with HAVING COUNT(NUM) = 1, and then applying MAX on the result. Q2 achieves the same by selecting a single row using ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 1 after the same GROUP BY and HAVING filter. Both are logically equivalent.
